how: Members call for a Vivec drawing and CHIM lettering, giving the room specific work to join.
A member answers the CHIM call with a bare commitment rather than a new request.
A member proposes Vivec and its location, while other members rally and accept work without an evidenced appointment to command.
Members propose the picture, repeated lettering, a border and a subreddit signature.
The organiser reports completion and another member reports adding a pixel to the third CHIM.
A clearer pixel-boundary reference and an anchor coordinate make the proposed work findable without proving the unseen template was followed.
The extra-account passage documents a recommendation, so actual added placements cannot be inferred without a report of use.
Recommending old alternate accounts is a preparatory step distinct from reporting their use or adjusting automated placements.
Practical instructions identify an organiser but cannot establish whether members decided an institutional order or never did so.
Members call for repairs, report interference and describe fixing colouring as placement ended.
A narrator attributes a replacement goal to opponents, but the live report names only someone and provides no documented attribution inquiry.
Neighbour appeals produce an agreed move and a change in where lettering is written.
Members yield the proposed location and redirect lettering rather than occupy the neighbours' requested space.
Anticipating another drawing's future overlap can prompt relocation before a loss is reported.
The initial move is explicitly explained by a neighbour's planned tribute, so loss-triggered retreat is unnecessary for that exchange.
A visitor offers spare pixels for exclamation points while asking that the cat remain intact.
A spare-pixel offer conditioned on availability establishes proposed help rather than completed reciprocal work.
A participant recounts an alliance placing CHIM, establishing a narrated coalition rather than independently verified formation or durability.
A visitor speaks for another room's cat and offers its potential help without evidence of formal appointment.
Respecting adjacent drumcorps space does not establish guest occupation under a host's rule.
Referral to another participating room does not show members disputing who can commit their room.
Members describe the pixels through CHIM and c0da, while a repair call recruits lore roles to defend the shrine.
The narrated dispute over CHIM establishes opposition during the event without establishing a quarrel predating it.
Lore names the proposed conversion target and replacement in the same turn without establishing a pre-existing feud with a named subreddit.
Members perform one-day food rules and a proposed subreddit takeover alongside canvas activity.
Parody rules about food and lore do not evidence restrictions, routing or moderation of canvas talk.
Members claim they did it, express pride and credit guards for keeping the image.
An achievement claim can be disputed, so celebration is observable even when the purported completed work remains unverified.
Members mark the end and describe the image as intact and its lettering as legible.
Post-event assessments of survival do not establish a successor canvas, reused emblem or continued organisation.
A recollection of fixing colouring as placement ended does not establish post-close cleanup or a contest over preserved versions.
Calls for help do not themselves say the room has too few hands or too little room.
Members propose converting the Skyrim logo into lore figures or lettering and one reports writing in its centre.
A participant narrates the dispute over replacing CHIM and another frames additional recruitment as marching into battle.

statement: testing whether a claimed canvas achievement happened
how: A direct fake-news challenge tests an earlier accomplishment claim rather than merely identifying or interpreting neighbouring art.

statement: following a seen mark back to its room
how: One person reports coming to the room immediately after seeing the artwork without establishing membership or the cause of that visit.
The call receives commitment, but no cited reply verifies completion caused by that call.
The proposal precedes a rally, but the rally does not explicitly attribute its motivation to the starter.
Completion reports and later repair calls establish a compatible sequence without establishing that reporting completion caused maintenance.
Maintenance pressure is one route into neighbour negotiation, but an explicit warning of future overlap also produces agreement before the coded defence calls.
A neighbour's request is explicitly accepted through relocation or redirected lettering, supporting agreement and restraint within the exchange.
The initial alt-account recommendation cannot be attributed to later maintenance strain, and no concept confirms actual use.
Completion and celebration coexist, but the untimed completion edit cannot establish their exact order or the proposed causal mechanism.
The final-canvas announcement receives replies evaluating survival, supporting a local finish-to-assessment transition without proving celebration caused archiving.
Survival assessments do not establish a subsequent decision to carry the temporary effort forward.
The explicit overlap warning and accepted relocation explain this move without a judgment of insufficient hands.
A reference and coordinates are shared, but no cited exchange shows a template resolving a prior design argument.
The call to write CHIM receives a bare commitment in its direct reply.
The help offer accompanies a cat-preservation appeal without evidence that maintenance strain caused the offer or that help arrived.
A contingent help offer can accompany the initial space appeal rather than follow a settled agreement or become delivered reciprocity.
Recruitment precedes conversion proposals, but no cited passage attributes attacking another mark to the recruitment call.
Yielding to drumcorps does not answer the distinct Skyrim conversion call, so it cannot establish an attack-to-restraint response.
The documented neighbour negotiation does not answer the Skyrim conversion proposal.
The Skyrim conversion and narrated CHIM contest concern different objects, so their coexistence cannot establish the proposed attack-to-rivalry link.
The narrated alliance lacks an evidenced formation sequence attributing coalition membership to maintenance pressure.
A canvas call and unrelated parody rules do not show that recruitment generated restrictions on canvas traffic.
An accepted cat request and referral to another participating room do not establish a subsequent dispute over binding authority.
